findings.title: V2 canManage() grants management from VIEW scope
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the V2 permission fallback uses hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Because the implementation returns true when the caller has the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource, an admin who was granted only view on all-groups will pass canManage() and therefore requireManage(). The only call site in this PR is GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, which would then let a view-only admin create new top-level realm groups, even though they are not allowed to update or delete groups (per-group requireManage(group) correctly checks only MANAGE). canManage() must check only the MANAGE scope, not VIEW. The per-group counterpart canManage(GroupModel) is implemented correctly and only requests AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

findings.title: Javadoc for canManage() documents the buggy behavior
findings.body: The new Javadoc on GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() states 'For V2 only: Also if it has permission to AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW or AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE groups.' This was added in this PR and matches the buggy GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() implementation, but the documented contract is wrong: VIEW on all-groups must not imply management. The contract for canView() right below it is correct (VIEW or MANAGE), reinforcing that canManage() should only require MANAGE. The Javadoc should be corrected to 'Also if it has a permission to AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE groups' so it does not codify the privilege escalation.

findings.title: No test for view-only on all-groups being denied for management
findings.body: The new GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest only covers granting MANAGE on all-groups (testManageAllGroups) and granting MANAGE/VIEW on individual groups. It never grants only the VIEW scope on all-groups and asserts that POST /admin/realms/{realm}/groups is forbidden. Because of the canManage() bug described above, that assertion would currently fail, so the test gap is what allowed the regression to slip in. A test granting only the all-groups VIEW scope and then calling add(new GroupRepresentation()) and expecting 403 would both document the intended contract and catch this bug.

findings.title: resolveGroup() never resolves by name/path while resolveUser() does
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() dispatches the GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE case to resolveGroup(), which only attempts session.groups().getGroupById(realm, id) and returns group.getId() verbatim. The sibling resolveUser() also falls back to session.users().getUserByUsername(realm, id) and resolveClient() falls back to getClientByClientId(...). The asymmetric handling means that if a caller passes a group name or path instead of the internal id (a plausible mistake when constructing policies), resolveGroup() will return null and getOrCreateResource() will throw IllegalStateException('Could not map resource object ...'). At minimum the method should attempt the by-name lookup for symmetry, or this limitation should be called out in the class Javadoc.

findings.title: canManage() lost its 'for V1 only' admin default fallback when V2 was added
findings.body: The diff replaced 'return root.users().canManageDefault()' in GroupPermissions.canManage() with 'return root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)'. canManageDefault() was removed from UserPermissions in the same PR. The change is semantically equivalent for the remaining caller, but it means GroupPermissionsV2 can no longer be re-entered through the old canManageDefault() hook. More importantly, callers that were updated to use root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS) directly (e.g. RolePermissions.canMapRole) no longer go through any wrapper that can be changed centrally. This is a minor maintainability concern, but it also means the previous 'canManageDefault' abstraction (which could one day include V2 logic) was removed in the same commit that added V2. Worth keeping in mind if V2 is later extended to model 'can manage users' differently.
